subtopics.title: The Cosine Rule and Where It Comes From

questions.question: In a² = b² + c² − 2bc·cosA, the side a and the angle A are always:
options: Both the largest in the triangle

questions.question: In the proof of the cosine rule, the two b² terms merge into one because:
When angle A = 90°, the cosine rule reduces to:
In the proof, after dropping the perpendicular from C onto AB at D, the length DB equals:

subtopics.title: Finding a Side — Two Sides and the Included Angle

questions.question: In triangle ABC with b = 8 cm, c = 5 cm and A = 60°, side a equals:
For an included angle of 110°, the correction term −2pr·cosQ becomes positive because:
options: Cosine of an obtuse angle is negative, and the two minus signs make a plus
The formula changes for obtuse angles

questions.question: With p = 6, r = 9 and Q = 110°, side q correct to two decimals is:
An obtuse-angle answer that comes out SHORTER than the right-angle version signals:
options: The sine rule should have been used
A sign was mishandled — a wider angle must push the far side longer

subtopics.title: Finding an Angle — Three Sides, No Angle

questions.question: In cosA = (b² + c² − a²)/2bc, the side that gets subtracted on top is:
options: Either of the sides next to angle A
The side opposite the angle being found

questions.question: For sides 5, 7 and 10 cm, the largest angle is found opposite the 10 because:
options: The largest angle always faces the longest side
The cosine rule only works on the longest side

questions.question: For sides 5, 7 and 10, cosθ = −26/70 gives θ equal to:
Inverse cosine has no 'second suspect' at 180° minus the answer because:
options: The calculator automatically tests both options
Obtuse angles cannot appear in triangles
cos(180° − θ) has the opposite sign, not the same value

subtopics.title: Two-Dimensional Problems — Harbours, Bearings and Shared Sides

questions.question: Boats sail 4 km and 6 km from harbour H with 70° between their courses. The distance between them is:
The cosine rule was chosen for the first calculation because triangle HPQ offered:
options: Two sides and the included angle — no complete opposite pair existed
A right angle at the harbour

questions.question: For the angle at P, the cosine rule was preferred over the sine rule because:
options: The sine rule cannot find angles at all
The cosine rule is quicker to type
The angle might have been obtuse, and inverse cosine settles that without ambiguity
The sine rule only works in right-angled triangles

questions.question: With angle H = 70° and angle P ≈ 71°, angle Q must be about:
In the two-friends picture, the final distance apart depends on the paths and on:
options: The walking speed of each friend
The angle at the corner where the paths begin

questions.question: A corner tighter than 90° means the friends end up:
options: Closer than the square-corner answer — the correction subtracts

questions.question: At exactly 90°, the correction term vanishes because:
The recommended calculator habit for the cosine rule is:
options: Round the cosine to one decimal before multiplying
Compute the correction term separately and subtract it by hand
Convert the angle to radians first
Type the whole right-hand side in one go and press equals once

questions.question: The first question to ask before choosing a rule is:
options: What do I hold in this triangle?
What does the final answer look like?
Which rule has the shortest formula?
Is the triangle drawn to scale?

questions.question: Holding two sides and the angle squeezed between them, the only rule that fits is:
Inverse sine is called the witness who cannot tell twins apart because:
options: It only works for angles below 45°
It gives a different answer each time
An acute angle and its 180°-minus partner have identical sines

questions.question: Writing the inventory sentence — 'two sides and the included angle are known, so the cosine rule applies' — is recommended because it:
options: Fills space in the answer book
Replaces the need for a sketch
Earns the method mark and stops the wrong formula before it starts

questions.question: In a two-triangle problem, the bridge is:
options: The longest side of the diagram
The side the two triangles share
The angle at the top of the sketch
The line of sight to the horizon

questions.question: The correct order of work is:
options: Solve both triangles simultaneously with one equation
Guess the shared side and check at the end
Solve the triangle where enough is known, find the shared side, then carry it into the second triangle
Always work in the triangle containing the unknown first

questions.question: Crossing the bridge with a ROUNDED value is dangerous because:
options: The rounding error poisons every number in the second triangle

questions.question: Before computing anything in a two-triangle question, you should:
options: Erase the given diagram and start again
Find every angle in both triangles
Circle the shared side and note which triangle gives it and which needs it
